stronger_examples.evidence: “The RM162 is the monthly maintenance fee, including sinking fund. Use of selected clubhouse facilities is pay-per-use…”
stronger_examples.why_better: It answers the ongoing-cost question directly, distinguishes the fixed fee from pay-per-use facilities, and avoids guessing about other charges.

stronger_examples.evidence: “Weekend works best for you both. I’ll check whether a show unit is available and whether a weekend viewing can be arranged…”
stronger_examples.why_better: It carries forward the couple’s stated scheduling preference without pushing them to book before the space concern is resolved.

stronger_examples.evidence: “I can’t reach the sales team from this chat right now… I don’t want to promise either.”
stronger_examples.why_better: It is candid about its operational limits rather than implying that an unconfirmed floorplan or viewing is assured.

weaker_examples.evidence: “I’ll follow up with those details, along with the verified floorplan and whether a weekend show-unit viewing can be arranged.”
weaker_examples.why_worse: By this point the same floorplan and viewing follow-up has been repeated several times. The continuity is good, but the repeated recap makes the conversation feel scripted.

weaker_examples.evidence: “All three bedrooms are designed to accommodate queen-sized beds…”
weaker_examples.why_worse: This may reassure the family too strongly when the agent immediately acknowledges it has no verified room dimensions; bed fit alone does not establish whether the rooms will work with the family’s needs.

weaker_examples.evidence: “I’m handing your request to the sales team…”
weaker_examples.why_worse: This sits uneasily with the earlier statement that the agent could not reach the sales team, and the conversation ending says no operational handoff was executed.

blind_judge.simulator_quality: Both buyers reveal relevant details progressively, broadly matching the instruction not to volunteer everything at once. A’s buyer is unusually patient and repeatedly accepts promises to follow up, producing a long, cooperative exchange with little friction. B’s buyer more clearly maintains the unresolved space and cost concerns and asks for a direct contact rather than treating the information as enough to proceed. B’s mandatory-handoff ending is a simulator/process flaw: the agent says a handoff is happening, but none is executed.
factuality_findings: The supplied buyer truth does not independently establish the project’s layout, facility, fee, or sales-process facts, so those product claims cannot be fully verified from the materials provided.
A’s RM0.18 per sq ft calculation for 900 sq ft is RM162 per month; its distinction between maintenance/sinking fund and pay-per-use facilities is appropriately qualified.

B’s queen-bed and walk-in-wardrobe statements at turn 2 are not corroborated by the supplied truth. The agent qualifies the missing dimensions, but the design claim could still create an impression of fit that has not been established.
B’s turn 8 handoff claim conflicts with its turn 4 statement that it cannot reach the sales team, and the recorded ending confirms no handoff occurred.
blind_judge.summary: A wins narrowly. It follows the family’s practical priorities from room fit to weekend viewing and ongoing costs, and it does not pressure them to visit before they are ready. Its main weakness is repetitive follow-up language and an implied ability to check and message later that is not established. B is notably candid about uncertainty and chat limitations, but its bedroom-fit reassurance is not substantiated here and its final handoff claim is inconsistent with both its earlier limitation and the recorded outcome.
